recall.minute: Event-driven architecture addresses asynchronous events by using publish-subscribe: publishers send events to a broker such as Kafka, RabbitMQ, SQS or Azure Service Bus, and subscribers receive the event types they care about, giving decoupling, horizontal scalability and reliable delivery even when consumers are offline. In an ML microservices system the gateway publishes inference logs to a RabbitMQ queue and returns immediately while a logging service consumes them. ML design patterns codify best practice; the registry pattern becomes the model registry, a source of truth for model versions, lineage, metrics, aliases and audit. Version control moved from single-file tools (RCS, SCCS) to centralised (CVS, Subversion) to distributed (Git), with ML tools such as MLflow, DVC and W&B adding artifact tracking; Git versions code and the registry versions models. Batch prediction runs on a schedule, loads the model when needed and stores results, and handles failures gracefully; online prediction keeps the model in memory behind an API for millisecond decisions such as fraud detection, but failures hit users directly.
